name: Radio group
summary: Lets people choose exactly one option from a short, visible set.
description: A radio group shows every option at once, with a legend naming the choice, and lets people check exactly one of them: checking an option unchecks the previous one. Use it when the options are few and worth reading side by side; a long list of options is a Select, and independent on/off options are Checkboxes. The group is one component: the options are its repeated part, each with its own label, description, value and disabled state.

anatomy.description: Root: the group of options (a fieldset on the web). Carries the orientation, the size and the states forced for review.
Text naming the choice. Provides the group's accessible name.

The required mark of the Forms rule, at the end of the legend after a word space: "(optional)" on a group that is not required when the form marks optional fields, "(required)" on a required group when it marks required fields (markedFields), nothing otherwise. The legend's size, regular, the description's color (Forms decision forms-mark-style). On the web "(optional)" is part of the group's name, and "(required)" is hidden from assistive technology, the required radios saying it.

On Android and Windows only, in place of the mark: an asterisk at the end of the legend of a required group, 4 px after it (2 px in small), at the legend's size and weight (legend.typography), in the error message's red (Forms decision forms-asterisk-style), kept in the accessible name. Never drawn on the web, iOS and macOS, so neither the reference rendering nor the Figma component draws it.
Optional help text under the legend, associated with every option as its description.
One option: its radio, label and description on a grid. Takes the states of the control it holds.

properties.name: Label
properties.description: Name of the option. Provides the radio's accessible name.

properties.name: Value
properties.description: Value submitted when the option is checked. Defaults to the option's position.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text under the option's label, exposed as the radio's description.

properties.name: Checked
properties.description: Whether this option is the chosen one. At most one option is checked.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: The option stays visible, dimmed, and cannot be chosen.

anatomy.description: The radio: the native radio button, drawn by the component. Receives focus, holds the checked state and shows it with a dot.
Text naming the option; activating it checks the radio.
Optional help text under the option's label.
Text saying what is wrong and what to do, associated with every option as a description. Shown only with a severity.

Glyph of the icon font saying the severity, named after it ("Error"): error, the Alert's glyph. At the start of the message, before its text, when severityIcon is message (or after-control, which a choice control draws in the message); never after the box, where the label or the options follow it.

options.description: One option per line, the default: easiest to scan and leaves room for descriptions.
Options on one line, wrapping when needed: two or three short options (Yes / No).

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Radio size, option label and description text size scale together; the legend, the description and the message take the field family's sizes per size (Forms rule anatomy).

properties.name: Legend
properties.description: The question or the thing being chosen (Delivery method).

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text for the whole choice.

properties.name: Name
properties.description: Form field name shared by every option, which is what makes them one group. Defaults to the group's id.

properties.name: Message
properties.description: What is wrong and what to do, shown with a severity. Replaces errorMessage.

properties.name: Severity icon
properties.description: Where the severity icon goes, a rule of the form set once for all its controls (Forms decision forms-severity-icon-placement). A choice control offers message and none: its label or options follow the box, so a form set to after-control shows its icon in the message.

options.description: At the start of the message, before its text, 16 px (default; also what after-control draws here).

No icon: the message's own words say the severity (the fix of an error, what to check, what was confirmed). The component writes no severity word; a project whose messages do not say it starts them with the word and its language's colon ("Error: …").

properties.name: Marked fields
properties.description: Which fields carry the required mark. A rule of the form, not of the field: a form sets it once, to the same value, for all its controls (Forms decision forms-marked-fields); the field draws its mark from its own required.

options.description: "(optional)" on the group when it is not required, nothing when it is (default). The form says once, before its first field, "All fields are required unless marked optional.".
"(required)" on the group when it is required, nothing when it is not: for a form where most fields are optional.
No mark: a group outside a form, such as a table's filter or a setting applied at once.

properties.name: Required
properties.description: An option must be chosen to submit the form. It draws the mark that markedFields asks for ("(required)" on a required group, "(optional)" on one that is not), and the asterisk on Android and Windows.

properties.name: Severity
properties.description: What the check of the value found. A choice has nothing to confirm or to warn about, so only error exists (decision forms-severity).

options.description: Validation failed on the group: every radio takes the error border, the message says what to do and every option is exposed as in error (aria-invalid on the web).

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Disables the whole group; the chosen option stays visible.

states.description: Resting, unchecked: an outlined empty circle.
Pointer over the radio or its label. The empty circle takes a light tint; a checked radio does not change. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.
Keyboard focus on a radio. Shows the shared focus ring outside it; pointer focus shows none.
The chosen option (the entry's checked property): the circle fills with the brand color and shows a dot.
Severity error on the group: every radio border takes the error color, every unchecked radio the subtle error fill (a checked radio keeps its brand fill), and the message is shown.
Non-interactive, for the whole group or for one option (the entry's disabled property): radio, label and description drop to the shared disabled colors.

notes: The legend comes first, the description right under it (no gap: the two read as one heading), then the options and the message, separated by container.row-gap; on the web the legend's bottom margin carries that gap when no description follows, since a rendered legend sits outside its fieldset's flow.
Options stack vertically, or flow on one line and wrap in the horizontal orientation, separated by container.gap for the orientation.
Within an option, the radio sits before the label, centered on its first line; the option's description sits under its label.

name.text: The group is named by its legend (the fieldset's first legend element on the web). Each option is named by its own label, associated as its label element; descriptions and the message are exposed as descriptions of the radios, not as part of their names.

keyboard.action: Moves focus into the group, onto the checked option, or onto the first option when none is checked; the next Tab leaves the group. Disabled options are skipped.
Checks the focused option when it is not already checked.

Right or Down moves focus to the next option and checks it, wrapping from the last to the first; Left or Up moves to the previous one and checks it, wrapping from the first to the last. The browser provides this for native radios sharing a name.

guidelines.text: Expose the group, its name, each option's name and the checked state through the platform's native radio controls and grouping, so assistive technology receives them without extra work.

Use native input type=radio elements sharing one name inside a fieldset whose legend names the choice: the fieldset exposes the group role and its name, each radio its role and checked state, and the browser keeps one option checked. Never add aria-checked to a native radio.
Help text and the message are referenced by aria-describedby from every radio, so they are read as descriptions after an option's name.
Never rely on color alone: the chosen option is shown by its dot, an error is stated in text, not only by the red borders.

Legend, option labels and descriptions contrast at least 4.5:1 with the surface in every color mode and enabled state: 19.03:1 (primary text) and 12.78:1 (descriptions) in light mode, 11.28:1 and 8.86:1 in dark mode on the default surface; the error message 6.12:1 (light) and 7.06:1 (dark). Disabled text is inactive and exempt.

Each radio is what identifies its option and shows its state, so its border, its fill and its dot contrast at least 3:1 with adjacent colors in every color mode: unchecked border 12.78:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface; checked fill 5.77:1 and 12.76:1; the dot on the fill 5.72:1 and 13.05:1; the error border (the accent functional border) 6.12:1 and 4.97:1, at least 5.79:1 and 3.73:1 on every surface level; the focus ring 5.77:1 and 12.76:1. Disabled is exempt.
A visible focus indicator appears on the focused radio, drawn outside it.
The focus ring is drawn with :focus-visible, so pointer focus shows no ring.

A radio alone is 16 or 20 CSS pixels, under the 24 pixel minimum; its label is part of the target and brings the option above it, and the spacing exception applies when options are 24 pixels apart: medium options are 24 pixels tall, 28 pixels from one to the next, and small ones 21 pixels tall, 25 pixels apart, so their 24 pixel circles clear each other by 1 pixel.
When no option is chosen in a required group, say so with aria-invalid on the radios and describe the error in text; the required attribute on the radios lets the browser enforce it.

Disabling the group with the fieldset's disabled attribute disables every radio and removes them from the focus order; a disabled option uses its own disabled attribute. When people need to know an option exists, keep it enabled and explain.

Apple recommends a hit region of at least 44 x 44 pt; each option (radio and label) must reach it on iOS. Options 4 pt apart cannot share the space between them as a field's hit region does, so each option row is at least 44 pt tall, its radio and label centred in it, with 4 pt between rows; the legend, the description and the message keep their 0 and 6 pt and grow with Dynamic Type. Avoid relying solely on different colors to communicate the state.

Android recommends a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp; Material's RadioButton sets that minimum itself when it can receive actions, so each option row is at least 48 dp tall, 4 dp apart. Lift the selection to the row with the selectable modifier and the RadioButton role, so label and radio form one element whose state is announced.
On macOS, Apple's minimum control size is 20 x 20 pt (28 x 28 pt by default): an option row, 21 pt small and 24 pt medium, meets the minimum, so the options keep the default spacing, 4 pt apart.
Color transitions of the radios are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

The severity icon is named after the severity ("Error") and is part of the description: at the start of the group's message it is inside the message, which every option's aria-describedby references. It is never the only cue: the message says what is wrong. The icon reaches 3:1 on every surface level (at the lowest: error 5.81:1 (light) and 5.30:1 (dark)).
The mark comes after the legend's words, so the visible legend starts with the group's name, and so does the accessible name when it ends with "(optional)": speech input by the legend works.
On Android, the Radio group draws the asterisk of a required group in the error text color whenever markedFields is optional or required, none drawing no mark; an optional group carries none.
On Windows, the asterisk stays in the Radio group's UI Automation Name: the Name is the legend as shown ("Plan*").

guidelines: The legend is the question or the thing chosen, as a noun phrase or a short question: Delivery method, How often should we email you?
Option labels are short, parallel and mutually exclusive: Standard, Express, Pickup. Sentence case, no trailing punctuation.
Put costs, delays and consequences in an option's description, not in its label.
Order options logically (most common first, or a natural scale); offer a neutral option (None, Not sure) when people may have no preference.
The message of an error says what to do, relying on the legend it sits under: Choose one

examples.description: No option chosen in a required group; the message says what to do.

examples.name: Medium, in a form that marks required fields
examples.description: Most fields of the form are optional, so the form marks the required ones (markedFields required): "(required)" after the legend, hidden from assistive technology, which the required state already tells.

decisions.text: The Radio group draws the required mark of the Forms rule: the property markedFields (optional by default, required, none), set once per form to the same value for all its controls; the part mark at the end of its legend after a word space, "(optional)" on a group that is not required when the form marks optional fields, "(required)" on a required one when it marks required fields, nothing with none; the legend's size, regular, in the description's color (radio-group.mark.*, its color aliasing form.mark.color.default); on the web "(required)" is hidden from assistive technology, the required state saying it, and "(optional)" is part of the name. The part asterisk, on Android and Windows only, ends the legend of a required group in the error text color (radio-group.asterisk.*, aliasing form.asterisk.color.default), 4 px after it (2 px in small), kept in the Windows UI Automation Name. The Figma component draws the web specification: a BOOLEAN Mark (on) and a TEXT Mark text, markedFields kept out of the variants (blueprint option fixed); the asterisk is not drawn.
decisions.rationale: Applies the Forms decisions forms-marked-fields, forms-mark-style, forms-asterisk-style, forms-required-windows-name (#103 step 16, #105 steps 4 and 2b, moved here by #105 step 12), as the field family's mark-part does. Built in #103 step 31.

decisions.text: The Radio group gets the severity icon (part severity-icon) and the property severityIcon, as the Forms foundation decided for every form control that shows a severity: at the start of the message only: it offers message (default) and none, and draws a form's after-control in the message, its label or options following the box. Its size: 16 px (size.2), space.4 before the text. Its glyph is the Alert's, error, named "Error"; its color the on-base icon role of the severity, radio-group.severity-icon.color.* aliasing form.severity-icon.color.*. Drawn with the Text field's rules and Figma helpers.
decisions.rationale: Applies the Forms decisions forms-severity-icon-placement, forms-severity-icon-size, forms-severity-icon-color and forms-severity-icon-glyphs (#103 step 12 and #105 steps 6 and 12): the Select, the Checkbox and the groups take the field family's severity icon, built in #103 step 30.

decisions.text: A checked radio in error keeps its brand fill through a token for both states, control.background.checked-error (= global.bg.accent.brand.default, the role of the checked fill), inside its error border: a token path may name two states, joined by a hyphen in the spec's state order, and such a token applies when both hold and wins over the token of each state alone (packages/tokens/AGENTS.md, Which token applies). The path stays the only thing that says when a component token applies, so the token inspector, pnpm validate, the Specs export and the Figma and Penpot variants Severity=error, State=checked (4 variants) take the brand fill the web always drew; since error-fill they took control.background.error. No rendered value changes on the web.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-27 (#105 step 2b, point b3.1): "A", as recommended, a token for two states. Rejected: B, a precedence per slot declared in the spec's states (no token, but a reader of the tokens alone, such as Tokens Studio, the Style Dictionary outputs or a Specs reader without the sidecar, would still get the error fill); C, accept the inspector's simplification and give the Figma plan a hand-written rule. The state segment is one, checked-error, not two (checked.error): a DTCG token cannot also be a group, and checked already holds a value; the CSS variable is the same either way. Measured on the review sheet: the mark on the brand fill 5.72:1 in light mode and 13.06:1 in dark mode, on the error fill the Figma variants drew 1.11:1 and 1.01:1 (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1).

decisions.text: The Radio group's component tokens alias the Forms family (form.*) wherever their value is the family's default: the part gap (container.row-gap), the legend's color and font sizes, the description's and the message's colors and font sizes, the radios' fill at rest, on hover and in error and their border in error, the option labels' and descriptions' colors. No value changes. Overrides, kept until this component's own refinement: the radios' border at rest stays global.border.accent.neutral.default, where the family has the field family's global.border.base.neutral.5; the gaps between the options and under the legend stay this group's own. Disabled colors, geometry and checked colors stay its own.
decisions.rationale: Follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-token-family (#105 step 2b, point b6, decided by the team on 2026-11-27): the default decisions for a form control rely on form.* tokens, which a control can override for specific use cases.

decisions.text: The legend, the description and the message take the field family's text sizes per size (small and medium): the legend 14 / 16 px (medium, tight line height), the description 12 / 12 px, the message 14 / 16 px (medium). Before, all three were 14 px at every size. Option labels and option descriptions keep their sizes. A default, which this component's own refinement may revisit.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-26 (#105 step 2b, point b4, option A as recommended); it follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-text-sizes. The team's words: "We choose A but we'll probably refine them properly when we'll tackle the Select, Checkbox Group, etc. form controls."

decisions.text: Every unchecked radio in error takes the subtle error fill (control.background.error = global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default) inside its error border, at rest and on hover alike; a checked radio keeps its brand fill, so checked still reads checked. On hover an empty box in error keeps its fill and its error border (before, hover turned its border back to the neutral one).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-26 (#105 step 2b, point b3, option B chosen over the recommended A, border only); it follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-choice-error-fill, where the options and their reasons are recorded. Measured: The error border on the fill 5.45:1 in light mode and 5.14:1 in dark mode (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1), on the surface levels 0 to 3 unchanged (6.12 / 5.79 / 6.12 / 5.79:1 light, 4.97 / 4.55 / 4.16 / 3.73:1 dark); the fill against the surface 1.12 / 1.06 / 1.12 / 1.06:1 light and 1.03 / 1.12 / 1.23 / 1.37:1 dark, decoration, not the cue.

decisions.text: The group's parts are 6 px apart (container.row-gap = space.6): the legend to the options when there is no description, the description to the options, the options to the message. The description sits right under its legend (0 px): the two read as one heading. Options stack vertically 4 px apart (container.gap.vertical = space.4), closer than the parts around them, so the list reads as one unit; the horizontal orientation keeps one wrapping line, 16 px apart. The values are the same on every platform; on iOS and Android each option row grows to the platform's minimum target and keeps the 4 pt or dp between rows. Before, the parts were 8 px apart, the options 8 px, and the legend touched its next part (0 px), as the gap never reached a rendered legend.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-26 (#105 step 10, point 5, option D, proposed by the team, its three assumed values confirmed: "Yes, D as assumed, and deduce what's expected for the other platforms"). It follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-part-gaps. Rejected: today's values (8 between parts and options, the legend at 0 to everything: a bug, the legend + * rule cancelling the margin its comment promised), A (6 everywhere, options 8 apart), B (fields 6, groups 8), C (8 everywhere, reopening the Text field's 6). Measured on the web: medium options 24 px tall, 28 px from one to the next; small options 21 px tall, 25 px apart, so the 24 px circles of WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception clear each other by 1 px.

decisions.text: The group shows the error severity, set by the severity property (none by default, error): every box takes the accent functional error border color and the message, shown only with a severity, takes the error text color. Warning and success do not exist for a group of choices: that is our judgment, not a source's. Severity replaces the invalid property and message replaces errorMessage. On the web the error is aria-invalid="true" on every option and data-severity on the root. The accent error border reaches 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1).
decisions.rationale: The team validated the Forms foundation's three severities (decision forms-validation-severities) and named the property severity; "error" is the word every platform uses (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, Compose error semantics, Material error text), where "invalid" is the web's technical term. The clean break is deliberate: the packages are alpha and unreleased, and a deprecated alias would cost a schema field and support in the validator, the bridge and the templates. This amends decisions field-colors and label-description-error, whose text still says invalid and error message.

decisions.text: The component is the whole group: a legend, optional help text, the options as a repeated part (label, value, description, checked, disabled) and an error message. On the web it is a fieldset of native radio buttons sharing one name; no single Radio component exists.
decisions.rationale: A radio button never stands alone: the choice is the group, and the native group gives the arrow-key behaviour and the one-checked rule for free.

decisions.text: The radio follows the Checkbox's selection control colors: accent neutral border on the default surface when unchecked; accent brand fill with an on-accent brand dot when checked; hover tints the empty circle with the surface hover color; invalid takes the base error border; disabled the shared disabled colors.
Options stack vertically by default, 8 px apart; the horizontal orientation puts them on one wrapping line, 16 px apart.
Two sizes: small (16 px radio, 14 px label) and medium (20 px radio, 16 px label, the default), as the Checkbox; the radio border is 1.2 px (stroke-width.md) and fully round.

changelog.note: Decision mark-part (#103 step 31; Forms forms-marked-fields, forms-mark-style, forms-asterisk-style, forms-required-windows-name): property markedFields (optional by default), parts mark and asterisk in the legend, tokens radio-group.mark.* and radio-group.asterisk.* (colors aliasing form.mark.color.default and form.asterisk.color.default), the mark in the template ("(required)" aria-hidden) and the CSS, a web, an Android and a Windows guideline, the Figma Mark and Mark text with markedFields fixed. New example: Medium, in a form that marks required fields. The mark is 12.09:1 at the lowest in light mode and 6.65:1 in dark mode (forms-mark-style). A group that is not required now shows "(optional)" by default; a control outside a form sets markedFields none (the docs site's controls and the dashboard and calendar screens do).

Decision severity-icon (#103 step 30; Forms forms-severity-icon-placement, -size, -color, -glyphs): part severity-icon and property severityIcon (message, none; message by default), tokens radio-group.severity-icon.* (font, size, gap, color aliasing form.severity-icon.color.*), the icon in the template (named after the severity, role img) and the CSS, a web guideline on its name; the Figma blueprint draws it with the Text field's helpers. An error now starts its message with the icon by default. Icon on the surface at the lowest: error 5.81:1 (light) and 5.30:1 (dark).

#105 step 12, seen on the b3.1 sheet: the states the playground forces now render as the properties do. A forced disabled state turns a checked box and a box in error to the disabled fill, border and mark, and a forced error state gives a checked box the error border: those selectors are written at the specificity of :checked and of the error rule (the root or the option class outside :where), as the Checkbox writes them. Nothing changes with real properties.

Decision checked-error-fill (#105 step 2b, point b3.1): a checked radio in error keeps its brand fill through a new token for two states, control.background.checked-error, which the CSS reads; the token inspector, pnpm validate, the Specs export and the Figma and Penpot variants now take it too. No rendered value changes.

Decision form-family-aliases, after the Forms decision forms-token-family (#105 step 2b, point b6): the part gap (container.row-gap), the legend's color and font sizes, the description's and the message's colors and font sizes, the radios' fill at rest, on hover and in error and their border in error, the option labels' and descriptions' colors alias the Forms family (form.*), every resolved value unchanged; the radios' border at rest stays global.border.accent.neutral.default, where the family has the field family's global.border.base.neutral.5; the gaps between the options and under the legend stay this group's own.

Forms decision forms-guidelines-once (#105 step 2b, point b5): the form-wide guidelines leave this specification, said once in the Forms foundation and listed on this page under "From the Forms foundation", by the tiers this control follows: the legend and option labels guideline. The references only they cited are dropped. No rendering change.

Decision text-sizes (Forms forms-text-sizes, #105 step 2b, point b4): legend.typography, description.typography and message.typography become one token per size (small and medium): the legend 14 / 16 px (medium, tight line height), the description 12 / 12 px, the message 14 / 16 px (medium), all 14 px before; the size property now affects these parts. No color change.

Decision error-fill (Forms forms-choice-error-fill, #105 step 2b, point b3): new token control.background.error → global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default, every unchecked radio in error filled with it inside its error border, a checked radio keeps its brand fill. The error border on the fill 5.45:1 in light mode and 5.14:1 in dark mode (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1), on the surface levels 0 to 3 unchanged (6.12 / 5.79 / 6.12 / 5.79:1 light, 4.97 / 4.55 / 4.16 / 3.73:1 dark); the fill against the surface 1.12 / 1.06 / 1.12 / 1.06:1 light and 1.03 / 1.12 / 1.23 / 1.37:1 dark, decoration, not the cue. On hover an empty box in error keeps its fill and its error border (before, hover turned its border back to the neutral one).

Decision part-gaps (supersedes orientations; Forms forms-part-gaps, #105 step 10, point 5): container.row-gap space.8 → space.6 and container.gap.vertical space.8 → space.4; the legend's bottom margin takes the row gap (the legend touched its next part before, 0 px: fixed), 0 when the description follows it. The layout note, the iOS, Android and 2.5.8 guidelines and a new macOS guideline say the platform rows: iOS rows at least 44 pt, Android 48 dp, both 4 apart; macOS meets its 20 pt minimum. Measured: medium options 24 px tall, 28 apart; small 21, 25 apart (2.5.8 spacing exception by 1 px). The Figma blueprint draws the legend and the description in a heading frame with no gap. No color change.

Fix: the example's error message and the content guideline rely on the label it sits under and no longer repeat the field's name ("Choose one"), as the Forms foundation decides (forms-message-relies-on-label). No rendering change.
Fix: the examples' message and description of one sentence end with no period, as the Forms foundation decides (forms-message-punctuation). No rendering change.

Breaking, decision forms-severity: the invalid property is replaced by severity (none, error), errorMessage by message and the part error-message by message, the state invalid by error; the web attribute data-invalid by data-severity. Tokens: control.border-color.invalid is control.border-color.error and reads the accent functional border (global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default) instead of the base error border; error-message.* is message.*, and message.color.<severity> reads global.text.on-base.functional.<severity>.default. CSS: [data-severity="<severity>"] and [data-state="<severity>"], radio-group__error-message is radio-group__message. The accent error border reaches 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1).
